claims.implemented: The public semantic API and development/native conformance evidence satisfy the listed acceptance criteria.
claims.partial: A tested foundation exists, but one or more acceptance criteria remain open.
claims.missing: No public semantic implementation satisfies the acceptance criteria.
claims.intentional-difference: Kit provides an equivalent product outcome through a documented simpler semantic model.

surface.definition: One static Workflow<T> model and one createWorkflow<T> implementation define typed input, result, state, Dependencies, Signals, Updates, Queries, Failures, memo, and search meaning.
surface.execution: The deterministic execute callback and asynchronous message handlers use ordinary portable TypeScript plus one context containing durable control-flow operations.
surface.dependency: Every other Program receives one typed Workflow Dependency with plain execution and update references, lifecycle operations, messages, visibility, and schedules.
surface.activity-provider: A Dependency provider receives stable invocation, attempt, heartbeat, cancellation, and deferred-completion context; Workflow product code still calls the Dependency operation directly.
surface.testing: The Workflow fixture exposes the same typed Dependency, virtual durable time, restart and crash injection, history replay, and Dependency substitution.
surface.adapter: Namespaces, task queues, worker placement, eager or local execution, pollers, deployment versions, codecs, persistence, observability export, and native scheduling are adapter configuration or host Dependencies.

intentionalDifferences.kit: Signals, Updates, and Queries are declared once in Workflow<T> and implemented once in createWorkflow<T>.
intentionalDifferences.reason: The static Feature factory already owns both type meaning and implementation, so separate global definitions and handler registration only duplicate identity.

intentionalDifferences.kit: Awaited asynchronous Dependency calls are durable Activities; local or eager execution is an adapter optimization.
intentionalDifferences.reason: Dependencies are already the single environment-interaction boundary, and a second proxy API would overlap it.

intentionalDifferences.kit: One typed Workflow Dependency accepts serializable {id, run?} execution references.
intentionalDifferences.reason: Plain references cross Program, process, language, and persistence boundaries without introducing a second protocol.

intentionalDifferences.temporal: workflow task queues, activity task queues, namespaces, workers, and deployment routing in application calls
intentionalDifferences.kit: Program placement, Dependency providers, and adapter configuration realize topology.
intentionalDifferences.reason: Placement can change without changing product meaning and therefore cannot be embedded in portable business logic.

intentionalDifferences.temporal: cron strings alongside calendar and interval schedules
intentionalDifferences.kit: One structured calendar and interval schedule model; cron is import-only.
intentionalDifferences.reason: Cron is a redundant, less type-safe spelling of schedule meaning.

intentionalDifferences.temporal: Nexus as another durable operation API
intentionalDifferences.kit: Typed Dependencies carry cross-service durable operations.
intentionalDifferences.reason: Timeout, cancellation, identity, and completion guarantees belong to a Dependency contract; a second communication primitive is unnecessary.

intentionalDifferences.temporal: Workflow Streams as a separate experimental package
intentionalDifferences.kit: Durable streaming is composed from typed Signals, Updates, Queries, state, and backpressure policy.
intentionalDifferences.reason: The experimental surface adds no irreducible coordination primitive and remains tracked until its guarantees stabilize.

domains.name: Workflow definition and determinism
acceptance: Workflow code is deterministic under replay.
Time, randomness, identifiers, errors, and every command-producing operation have defined portable semantics.
Unsupported TypeScript fails compilation with an exact source diagnostic.
The semantic Workflow identity is authored once and survives refactoring.

domains.name: Start and execution lifecycle
acceptance: Start supports stable Workflow and run identity.
Start delay, Workflow timeouts, retries, reuse, and conflict policies are explicit.
Result following across Continue-As-New and retry chains is defined.
Cancel, terminate, reset, describe, and history operations have distinct guarantees.

domains.name: Durable Activities through Dependencies
acceptance: Awaited asynchronous Dependency calls receive durable Activity semantics without a second environment-interaction API.
Task queue, retry, cancellation, idempotency, and schedule-to-start, start-to-close, schedule-to-close, and heartbeat timeouts are represented.
Heartbeat details survive retry and worker loss.
Asynchronous completion, heartbeat, and failure are durable and idempotent where they close an attempt; external cancellation acknowledgement and local execution policy have explicit semantics.
Activity failures retain typed details and retry classification.

domains.name: Timers and durable conditions
acceptance: Relative and absolute timers survive process and authority downtime.
Conditions can wait on durable state with optional timeout.
Timers can participate in deterministic races and cancellation.
Timer replacement and replay compatibility are defined.

domains.name: Durable concurrency and cancellation scopes
acceptance: Parallel, race, and all-settled composition replay deterministically.
Nested cancellable and non-cancellable scopes have explicit propagation.
Branch failure and cancellation preserve deterministic command ordering.
Randomized interleavings produce equivalent JavaScript and Rust histories.

domains.name: Signals and external messages
acceptance: Signals are durable, typed, ordered, and asynchronous.
Synchronous and asynchronous handlers have defined initialization, buffering, and unfinished policies.
Workflows can signal other Workflows through the same typed Workflow Dependency.
Signal-with-start is idempotent and atomic at the durable authority.

domains.name: Queries
acceptance: Queries are typed and cannot mutate Workflow state or emit durable commands.
Consistency, worker availability, and closed-execution behavior are explicit.
Query execution is equivalent in JavaScript and native production.

domains.name: Updates
acceptance: Updates are typed, durable, state-mutating requests with typed results or failures.
A synchronous validator may reject before history acceptance.
Accepted and completed lifecycle stages are observable.
Update-with-start is idempotent and atomic.
Asynchronous handler completion and unfinished policy are defined.

domains.name: Child Workflows
acceptance: A Workflow can start or execute another statically known typed Workflow.
Child start acknowledgement, result, signal, update, query, cancel, and terminate semantics are durable.
Parent-close and child-cancellation policies are explicit.
Parent completion cannot race an unrecorded child start.

domains.name: Durable schedules
acceptance: Schedules support interval, calendar, and cron-compatible specifications.
Time zones, daylight-saving gaps and folds, jitter, exclusions, start, and end boundaries are deterministic.
Overlap, catch-up, misfire, and pause behavior are explicit.
Create, get, list, update, pause, resume, trigger, backfill, and delete are typed.
Schedule firing is idempotent across authority crashes and replicas.

domains.name: Continue-As-New and history bounds
acceptance: A Workflow can atomically complete one run and start the next with typed input.
Workflow identity and run-chain identity remain distinct.
History size and count limits are enforced before unsafe growth.
Compaction and retention preserve required replay and operational evidence.

domains.name: Workflow and worker versioning
acceptance: Patch markers allow compatible command-sequence changes.
Representative histories are replayed before release.
Worker deployment versions route old and new executions safely.
Retirement rules prove no retained execution still requires removed code.

domains.name: Visibility and search attributes
acceptance: Workflow memo and typed search attributes are distinct.
Running Workflows can upsert supported search attributes.
List, count, and filter operations have stable typed semantics.
Visibility projections are rebuildable and do not become Workflow authority.

domains.name: Namespaces, task queues, priority, and fairness
acceptance: Namespace identity and retention boundaries are explicit.
Workflow and Activity task queues support independent worker placement.
Priority, fairness, poller count, and backpressure are configurable without changing product logic.
Queue and namespace metadata lower consistently to development and production adapters.

domains.name: Data conversion and payload protection
acceptance: All durable inputs, results, state, messages, failures, and heartbeat details use versioned codecs.
Schema evolution and decoding failures have precise diagnostics.
Payload compression and encryption can be supplied behind Dependencies without changing Workflow code.
JavaScript and Rust codecs pass the same corpus.

domains.name: Operational controls
acceptance: Describe, history, cancel, terminate, reset, retry, and bulk controls expose typed semantics.
Backlog, rate limit, retention, and worker availability are inspectable.
Administrative operations are auditable and idempotent where required.

domains.name: Testing, time skipping, and replay
acceptance: Tests can skip durable time without sleeping.
Activities can be tested with heartbeat, cancellation, and retry context.
Representative and generated histories replay in JavaScript and Rust.
Crashes can be injected before and after every durable boundary.
Bulk history replay is a release gate.

domains.name: Logs, metrics, traces, and interception
acceptance: Workflow, Activity, worker, queue, and authority events have stable correlation.
Replay does not duplicate externally visible logs or metrics unintentionally.
Interception can add cross-cutting policy without bypassing durable semantics.
Backpressure, retries, timer lateness, and failure classes are measurable.

domains.name: Cross-service durable operations
acceptance: The parity review decides whether typed Dependencies already provide the equivalent product outcome.
If an intentional difference is claimed, cancellation, timeout, caller identity, durable completion, and cross-namespace behavior remain covered.
No second generic communication mechanism is introduced without a demonstrated semantic gap.

domains.name: Workflow-hosted durable streams
acceptance: The experimental Temporal surface is tracked separately from stable parity.
Any Kit implementation composes from Signals, Updates, Queries, and durable state rather than introducing an overlapping primitive.
Backpressure, ordering, retention, cancellation, and replay semantics are explicit.

domains.name: Horizontal scaling and failover
acceptance: Unrelated executions scale independently while one authority owns each mutable execution transition.
Workflow and Activity task placement scales independently.
Worker and authority crashes do not lose acknowledged durable commands.
Shard movement, lease expiry, partitions, and backpressure have production evidence.

domains.name: Generated native production
acceptance: Application and Feature-specific Workflow logic requires no handwritten Rust.
Generated Rust uses typed schemas and direct control flow for product logic.
The native durable executor is generic adapter infrastructure.
JavaScript and Rust execute the same Workflow IR and conformance corpus.
Complete generated multi-Feature executables pass restart and multi-process tests.

domains.name: Performance and capacity evidence
acceptance: Equivalent workload, durability, payload, persistence, and hardware assumptions are published.
Activity, signal, child, timer, history-growth, schedule, and mixed workloads are covered.
Throughput, tail latency, replay, recovery, memory, CPU, allocation, I/O, history size, binary size, and build time are recorded.
Regression budgets distinguish executor, single-node durable, and multi-replica tiers.
